subject: belly button
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Belly Button?

scenes.text: What if you never cleaned your belly button? You'd be growing a tiny rainforest.
When scientists swabbed about 60 navels, they found 2,368 kinds of bacteria.
Most belly buttons held around 67 types, and over 1,400 may be new to science.
One volunteer who said he hadn't washed in years carried two species known from ice caps and thermal vents.
Left for years, skin oil and dead skin can even harden into a dark navel stone.
The twist: one science writer carried a microbe only ever found in soil in Japan. He had never been there.

description:
What if you never cleaned your belly button? The Belly Button Biodiversity project at North Carolina State University swabbed about 60 navels and found 2,368 bacterial species, around 67 per person, with 1,458 possibly new to science. A man who had not washed in years hosted extremophiles usually found in ice caps and thermal vents.
In rare cases sebum and keratin build up into an omphalolith, a navel stone that can go unnoticed for years. Not medical advice.
